[Overview](https://usenaive.ai/docs) [Managed Agents](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/agents) [API Reference](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/overview) [SDK Reference](https://usenaive.ai/docs/sdk/typescript) [CLI Reference](https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/overview)

Zero to a running agent in five steps. Every command on this page is tested verbatim against a live deploy.

1

Install the CLI

```
npm i -g @usenaive-sdk/cli
naive --version
```

Upgrading from `@usenaive-sdk/vetta-cli`? Run `npm rm -g @usenaive-sdk/vetta-cli` first, because both
packages install the same commands. Your saved login carries over.

Prefer not to install it globally? Every command below also works as
`npx @usenaive-sdk/cli …`.The snippets below use `jq` to capture ids from JSON output (`… | jq -r .id`) — install it,
or copy the `agt_...` / `ses_...` ids from the output by hand.Working with a coding agent? Point it at the onboarding manifest —
[https://usenaive.ai/skill.md](https://usenaive.ai/skill.md) — and it will walk your operator
through everything on this page. Every command below is also a REST call against
[the API](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/overview), so `curl` works before the CLI does.

2

Authenticate

The CLI stores a **profile** — a credential plus base URL — and never prints it back.

```
read -rs KEY && printf '%s\n' "$KEY" | naive login   # an API key, piped so it stays out of shell history
naive login --email you@example.com --password '…'   # a person: signs in, stores a session token
```

Confirm which organization you are pointed at before you spend anything:

```
naive whoami
```

`NAIVE_API_KEY` and `--api-base-url` override the stored profile for a single command, so
scripts and CI never need a config file at all.

3

Start the plan

A new organization needs a plan before anything outside billing answers. Standard is $20 a
month with $20 of credit included, and starts with a 7-day free trial (card required); Pro is
$200 a month with $200 included. `subscribe` prints a hosted checkout link.

```
naive plan subscribe                # Standard; add --plan pro for Pro
naive plan show                     # status: active once the checkout completes
```

See [Pricing](https://usenaive.ai/docs/platform/pricing#plans).

4

Add credits

Billing is real US dollars, prepaid; the plan’s included credit lands here too and rolls over.
`topup` prints a hosted checkout link — nothing is credited until the payment settles.

```
naive credits topup --usd 50        # prints a hosted checkout link
naive credits show
```

Your organization is the billing entity; every agent draws from the same balance. See
[Billing](https://usenaive.ai/docs/platform/billing).

5

Create an agent

An agent bundles a model, a system prompt, a completion window, and a budget — the budget is
required, so every agent has a spend cap from birth.

```
AGENT=$(naive agent create \
  --name nightly-triage \
  --model z-ai/glm-5.3-flash \
  --budget-usd 50 --max-task-usd 5 --budget-period month \
  --window immediate \
  --system "You are a concise triage agent. You have a Linux sandbox. Do the work, then answer in one short paragraph." \
  | jq -r .id)

echo "$AGENT"     # agt_...
```

Later commands take the **id**, not the name. `naive models list` prints the model ids and the
completion windows each supports.

**You do not attach a computer to an agent.** Each agent gets its own computer the first time
one of its sessions’ tools needs it, and every session of the agent works on it and sees the
same files — a text-only agent never gets one and pays nothing for it.

6

Run it and stream the output

A session is one directly-controlled run: create it with its first message, then stream events.

```
SID=$(naive session create \
  --agent "$AGENT" \
  --message "Create notes.md in your home directory containing 'hello from naive', read it back, and tell me what it says." \
  | jq -r .id)

naive session stream --session "$SID"
```

The stream is the whole truth of the run — every model call with its quote, every tool call,
the reply, the usage line:

```
{"seq":4,"type":"tool.started","data":{"name":"write","args":{"path":"~/notes.md","content":"hello from naive"}}}
{"seq":5,"type":"tool.completed","data":{"name":"write","output":"Successfully wrote 16 bytes","is_error":false}}
{"seq":13,"type":"message.completed","data":{"role":"assistant","content":"Done — notes.md contains exactly: hello from naive."}}
{"seq":14,"type":"session.usage","data":{"consumed_micro_usd":2023,"active_seconds":7,"tool_calls":2}}
{"seq":15,"type":"session.idle","data":{"stop_reason":"end_turn"}}
```

Follow up with `naive session send --session "$SID" --text "…"`; resume a dropped stream with
`--after-seq`.

7

Read the meter

Every dollar is metered per component, per agent, and per session.

```
naive agent spend "$AGENT" --by component
naive session usage --session "$SID"
```

Files the agent published during the run are listed with
`naive file list --scope session --session "$SID"`.

## [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/quickstart\#create-an-api-key-for-programmatic-access)  Create an API key for programmatic access

Code authenticates with a **scoped API key** — the secret is returned once and never again:

```
naive keys create --name quickstart --scopes agents:read,agents:write,sessions:read,sessions:write
export NAIVE_API_KEY="sk_...the secret shown once..."
```

From TypeScript, use the key with the [TypeScript SDK](https://usenaive.ai/docs/sdk/typescript). It is ESM-only: set
`"type": "module"` in `package.json` (or use `.mts` / `.mjs` files), or load it with
`await import("@usenaive-sdk/managed-agents")` inside an async function in a CommonJS project (if `tsc`
builds it, set `"module"` to `"node16"` or `"nodenext"`, or tsc turns the import into `require()`).

## [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/quickstart\#driving-a-sandbox-directly)  Driving a sandbox directly

A computer is a disposable Linux sandbox you can drive yourself, independently of any agent.
Pause it and it bills nothing. Sessions work on their agent’s own computer — a computer you create
here is never handed to one. See the [Computer reference](https://usenaive.ai/docs/computer/index).

```
naive computer create --name box --vcpu 2 --memory-mb 4096 --disk-gb 20
naive computer exec cmp_... --command 'ls -a ~'
naive computer pause cmp_...
```

## [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/quickstart\#the-same-arc-over-http)  The same arc over HTTP

The CLI is a thin client over the REST API; the whole arc above is a few requests.

```
export NAIVE_API_KEY="sk_..."
export BASE="https://api.vetta.sh"

AGENT=$(curl -sS "$BASE/v1/agents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NAIVE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "nightly-triage",
    "model": "z-ai/glm-5.3-flash",
    "window": "immediate",
    "system": "You are a concise triage agent.",
    "budget": { "cap_micro_usd": 50000000, "max_task_micro_usd": 5000000, "period": "month" }
  }' | jq -r .id)

SESSION=$(curl -sS "$BASE/v1/sessions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NAIVE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"agent_id\": \"$AGENT\", \"message\": \"Summarize what you can see in your sandbox.\"}" \
  | jq -r .id)

curl -sN "$BASE/v1/sessions/$SESSION/stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $NAIVE_API_KEY"
```

See the [API overview](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/overview) for auth, pagination, idempotency and the shared error envelope.
